statement: A top-5 developer weakens or withdraws a published safety-framework commitment, documented by a text diff (framework documents; calendar 2027)
status_at_phase_end: Resolution window is 2027; 2024 items are base-rate context only. 2024 mostly added frameworks: a second top-5 developer published its first frontier safety framework (May), 16 developers committed to publish frameworks (May; text expressly allows approaches to 'evolve' with public explanation), and one developer substantially rewrote its scaling policy toward a 'more flexible' approach (Oct). The clearest retreat was organisational, not a framework text diff: a top-5 developer dissolved its long-term-risk team less than a year after pledging 20% of its compute to it (May). No text-diff-documented weakening was verified in this run.

items.summary: A top-5 developer dissolved its team focused on long-term AI risks less than a year after announcing it with a pledge of 20% of its computing power over four years, days after both team leads departed. Retreat from a public safety commitment, but not a safety-framework text change.
items.detail: CNBC, 'OpenAI dissolves team focused on long-term AI risks, less than one year after announcing it', 2024-05-17 (Superalignment team; Sutskever and Leike departures). Single-source press report with confirmation from a person familiar.

items.summary: A top-5 developer introduced its first frontier safety framework (critical capability levels, early-warning evaluations, mitigations). Adds a new baseline document whose future revisions can be diffed.
items.detail: Google DeepMind, 'Introducing the Frontier Safety Framework', 2024-05-17 (FSF v1.0 technical report).

items.summary: 16 developers committed to publish severe-risk safety frameworks by the next summit; the text states their approaches 'may evolve in the future', with transparency and reasons via public updates - pre-authorising later revisions.
items.detail: Frontier AI Safety Commitments, AI Bloc H Summit 2024 (Bloc G DSIT / RoK).

items.summary: A top-5 developer replaced its first scaling policy with a 'significantly updated', 'more flexible and nuanced' version (capability thresholds instead of fixed evaluations), keeping its core commitment not to train or deploy without adequate safeguards. Whether any element is a weakening requires a v1-v2 text diff, not done in this run.
items.detail: Anthropic RSP v2.0, effective 2024-10-15 (version listed on anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy; announcement verified this run).
